newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT -Dlr upside not lost if key supports hold.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT -Dlr upside not lost if key supports hold.

text.p: After a much-needed consolidation, the dollar is ready to retest its recent highs and conquer higher ground from there, analysts said on Thursday.

They pointed out the dollar has retained momentum as it kept on setting higher lows for five straight sessions since last Friday. The dollar/mark low on Thursday was 1.7860 versus 1.7456 a week earlier on July 10.
In late trade, dollar/mark was quoted at 1.7910/15 versus 1.7950/60 at the open and dollar/yen at 115.85/90 vs. 116.15.25.
Dollar/yen has also set higher lows since July 7 when it dipped to 111.90. Its low on Thursday was 115.68.

"Dollar/yen tested yesterday and today again a rising trendline from September 1995 that comes in at 116.50. Another big level after that remains the May 28 high of 117.00," said I.D.E.A. analysts Ben Morden.

"That level will probably determine whether we'll see 120.00 yen again," added Morden who said the dollar/yen upside remains intact unless violation of support at "114.50, the trigger level for the rally on Tuesday" that led to the recent high of 116.48 set on Wednesday.
The 117.00-yen level is also important as the 38-percent retracement of the fall from the year's high of 127.46 set on May 1 to the year's low of 110.62 on June 11.

Meanwhile, dollar/mark remains bullish, comfortably holding above 1.7850 support, with little meaningful resistance on the way to 1.8025, a prior objective, and 1.8040, the 71-month high set on Tuesday.
"I really see 1.8430 on dollar/mark medium term," said Morden, referring to the cycle high of July 1991. The prior high dates back to November 1989.
A sterling/mark rebound should help dollar/mark.

"The risk was that sterling/mark would lose big support at 2.9760, but it did not," Morden said of the sterling/mark correction that followed the high set on Monday. "I still like the view that we'll make 3.0575, the decade high."
However, cable is weakening after loss of support at $1.6815, a key retracement level.
Meanwhile, mark/yen consolidated in a reversal of the slide that took that cross to a recent low of 63.40. Main resistances at 65.25 and 65.55 remain to be taken out.
Dollar/Swiss continued to send positive signals for dollar/mark, with 1.4850, the recent high set on Wednesday, a key hurdle on the way to a retest of 1.4922, the 1997 high.
